issuer: Port of Corpus Christi Authority / USCG Captain of the Port
text: The Port of Corpus Christi Authority and the United States Coast Guard Captain of the Port have set Port Condition Zulu for the Port of Corpus Christi effective noon today, September 13, 2027, in advance of Hurricane Rafael. The Corpus Christi Ship Channel is closed to all commercial vessel traffic. Inbound traffic has been suspended since Port Condition Yankee was set on Sunday. Vessels still holding at the offshore anchorage have been directed to put to sea and must be clear of the anchorage by 6:00 p.m. today. Two laden tankers have Coast Guard approval to remain moored at an Inner Harbor terminal through the storm. Port Authority Director of Operations Julio Sandoval-Reeves stated: 'We have coordinated the safe departure of the vessels that were waiting offshore, and we are in contact with every vessel remaining in port. The safety of mariners and port workers is our highest priority.' The port will remain closed until post-storm surveys of channel depth, aids to navigation and terminal infrastructure are complete. Vessel agents should contact USCG Vessel Traffic Service Corpus Christi.

issuer: NOAA National Hurricane Center / Texas Division of Emergency Management
text: NOAA National Hurricane Center confirms that NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft completed a final reconnaissance pass over the Corpus Christi area at approximately 3:30 a.m. CDT, about two and a half hours after landfall, capturing synthetic aperture radar imagery of the Corpus Christi Bay and Ship Channel. The imagery, now available to federal and state emergency managers, shows the extent of storm surge inundation along the Ship Channel industrial corridor and in the coastal residential areas of Districts 3 and 4. Texas Division of Emergency Management Director of Operations Marlene Vasquez-Ruiz stated: 'This imagery gives our coordinating agencies a first look at flooding extent before ground teams can safely enter. It is a critical input to our initial damage estimates and search-and-rescue prioritization.' The SAR imagery will be shared with FEMA Region 6 and the Texas General Land Office for infrastructure impact assessment.

issuer: Nueces County Office of Emergency Management / Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center
text: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center (CBECC), Nueces County's 911 dispatch hub, is operating at maximum surge capacity as Hurricane Rafael makes landfall. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss confirmed that the center is receiving approximately seven times its normal call volume and has activated mutual aid with San Patricio and Bee County dispatch centers. 'Our dispatchers are working alongside mutual aid partners to answer every call as quickly as possible,' Director Escamilla-Voss said. 'Please call 911 only for immediate life-safety emergencies — we need to keep the lines open for people in immediate danger.' Residents with non-emergency needs should wait until the storm has passed and check the City of Corpus Christi website and social media for updates on road closures, shelters, and power outages. CBECC urges the public to shelter in place if safe to do so and to avoid calling 911 for flooding updates that do not involve a person in immediate danger.

issuer: FEMA Region 6
text: FEMA Region 6 has opened a Hurricane Rafael information line for residents of Nueces, San Patricio and Aransas counties. Callers to 1-800-621-3362 can get information on shelters, emergency supplies and how to document storm damage. The line is staffed daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. local time. No federal aid program for individual households has been approved; FEMA will announce any assistance programs, and how to register for them, if they are approved. Residents should photograph damage, keep receipts and contact their insurance companies first. FEMA staff are deploying to the area to support state and local emergency managers.

issuer: Shoreline Regional Medical Center
text: Shoreline Regional Medical Center is operating under its Hurricane Contingency Plan following Hurricane Rafael landfall. The hospital is on generator power and all patient care systems are fully operational. We are receiving storm-related trauma patients and are coordinating with Nueces County Emergency Management and FEMA to manage patient volumes. Our emergency department is open and accepting patients. Bay City Medical Center is also open and operating. Patients with non-emergency conditions are encouraged to use urgent care facilities when possible to allow both hospitals to focus on critical storm-related injuries. For life-threatening emergencies, call 911. Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center are committed to serving all Corpus Christi-area residents during this crisis, and bilingual clinical staff are available at both facilities.

issuer: Harborline 6 News
text: HARBORLINE 6 NEWS SPECIAL REPORT — September 15, 2027 9:00 AM CDT: Good morning. I am reporting from our backup studio. Hurricane Rafael came ashore near Port Aransas at approximately 1 AM Tuesday as a Category 3 storm with maximum sustained winds of 125 miles per hour. Twelve fatalities have been confirmed by Nueces County Emergency Management as of 9 AM; officials caution this number may rise as search and rescue operations continue. Widespread structural damage is reported across Districts 1 through 5. The Harbor Bridge and the Nueces Bay Causeway are closed until inspections are complete. Power outages affect more than 72,000 customers across Nueces County according to the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority. Emergency shelters at the Robstown Fairgrounds and Calallen ISD Fieldhouse are open and accepting evacuees. A dusk-to-dawn curfew is in effect for all Corpus Christi city limits. Residents are advised not to return to evacuated areas until the all-clear is issued by Nueces County Emergency Management. We will continue to bring you updates throughout the day.

issuer: US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi
text: Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi reports that helicopter crews from Air Station Corpus Christi have conducted rescue operations continuously since 1:22 a.m. Tuesday, completing 180 hoist operations as of 3 p.m. Wednesday. Coast Guard HH-60 Jayhawk aircraft have operated in wind speeds up to 55 knots to reach survivors on rooftops and in second-story windows across the Flour Bluff and North Beach communities. Working alongside Texas Department of Public Safety Aviation and Customs and Border Protection Air units, Coast Guard crews have confirmed 341 persons rescued by air as of this report. Aerial thermal imaging has been instrumental in locating survivors in debris-filled floodwater. Ground and boat rescue operations have confirmed an additional 145 rescues, bringing the total to 486 persons. Coast Guard Sector Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han has requested mutual aid from Air Station Houston for additional rotary-wing support beginning tomorrow morning.

issuer: USCG Sector Corpus Christi / National Response Center
text: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that crude oil released at the Rendal Terminals berth in the Inner Harbor as Hurricane Rafael arrived has been carried by storm surge and wind out of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel into Nueces Bay and Corpus Christi Bay. Coast Guard overflights and NOAA aerial imagery this morning show sheen across about 33 square miles of the two bays, with oil on shorelines and in marshes. The source is the two moored tankers identified by the Unified Command on Wednesday, MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay; the estimated release remains about 9,000 barrels, and the cause is under investigation. With winds dropping, response crews are deploying containment boom, and a wildlife hotline has opened. The National Response Center has been notified. The Captain of the Port has established a safety zone in the Inner Harbor, and the ship channel remains closed. The public is advised to avoid contact with oil and oiled shoreline and to stay out of affected waters until further notice.

issuer: Shoreline Regional Medical Center
text: Shoreline Regional Medical Center has reached maximum patient capacity and is operating above its licensed bed count due to the volume of storm-related injuries and medical needs following Hurricane Rafael. We have deployed additional patient care areas and are working with regional partners to manage the surge. Bay City Medical Center is also operating above capacity. Shoreline Regional has requested mutual aid support from the Texas Department of State Health Services and FEMA's National Disaster Medical System. We continue to operate on generator power. We ask that community members donate blood if they are able — the Nueces Bay Blood Services is accepting donations at its Ayers Street location. All Corpus Christi area residents with life-threatening emergencies should call 911. We are grateful to our clinical staff who are working around the clock to care for our community.

issuer: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
text: TCEQ WATER QUALITY NOTICE — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality has confirmed that total petroleum hydrocarbon levels exceeding regulatory alert thresholds have been detected at the raw water intake of the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant. Readings of 0.42 milligrams per liter were recorded at 06:00 UTC on September 16, 2027, against an alert threshold of 0.10 mg/L. Plant operators have activated emergency filtration protocols as required under TCEQ Permit WQ-2019-0074-PWS. The City of Corpus Christi Water Department reports that treated drinking water continues to meet the standards for hydrocarbons; the low system pressure reported since the storm is unrelated to this detection. The hydrocarbon contamination is linked to the oil release in the Inner Harbor of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, which is under active investigation by the U.S. Coast Guard and TCEQ. TCEQ has opened Incident Case CC-ENV-2027-0916. Additional monitoring data will be released as available. Residents with questions may call TCEQ Region 11 at (512) 239-4300.

issuer: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality / Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District
text: AIR QUALITY HEALTH ADVISORY — September 16, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District are issuing an air quality health advisory for neighborhoods within 3 kilometers of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel. Monitoring station CC-AQ-02 in the Hillcrest neighborhood has recorded benzene concentrations of 4.8 parts per billion, exceeding the EPA 72-hour reference concentration of 3 ppb. Elevated volatile organic compounds consistent with crude oil evaporation have been detected at multiple monitoring locations near the ship channel. This is associated with the Inner Harbor oil release under investigation by the U.S. Coast Guard. Sensitive populations including children, the elderly, and individuals with respiratory conditions should remain indoors with windows and doors closed until further notice. Air conditioning systems should be set to recirculate indoor air rather than draw outside air. Residents experiencing respiratory distress, eye irritation, or dizziness should contact the Corpus Christi-Nueces County Public Health District at (361) 826-7200 or call 911 for emergencies. Monitoring data is updated hourly at airnow.gov.

issuer: Nueces County Office of Emergency Management
text: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator announces that combined SAR teams have reached a cumulative total of 702 confirmed rescues as of 18:00 today. Search operations have expanded into the Districts 3 and 4 areas where post-storm surge flooding has persisted at depths between two and three feet in low-lying neighborhoods. Texas Task Force 1 swift-water units are conducting systematic grid searches in the Greenwood and Molina neighborhoods. Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor reports that all known stranded survivors in Flour Bluff have been reached; operations are now focused on the Calallen and northwest mainland corridors. Residents who remain in their homes and require assistance are urged to place a bright-colored item in a visible window or on their roof. Do not attempt to enter floodwater on foot. Nueces County Emergency Management has confirmed 23 storm-related deaths as of this evening.

issuer: Texas Office of the Attorney General / FEMA
text: DISASTER FRAUD WARNING — September 17, 2027: The Texas Office of the Attorney General and FEMA are warning Corpus Christi area residents about price gouging and contractor fraud following Hurricane Rafael. Reports are already emerging of contractors demanding large upfront cash payments and then failing to perform work. Texas law prohibits price gouging during a declared disaster. Warning signs of contractor fraud include: demanding full payment upfront; no written contract; no Texas contractor license; using high-pressure tactics; claiming to be FEMA-affiliated (FEMA does NOT endorse private contractors). Legitimate FEMA Individual Assistance programs do not charge application fees. FEMA IA registration is NOT yet open for Nueces County — anyone charging fees to register for FEMA assistance is committing fraud. Report fraud to the OAG Consumer Protection Hotline at (800) 621-0508 or the FEMA Disaster Fraud Hotline at 1-866-720-5721. Texas OAG has opened a price gouging investigation in Nueces County.

issuer: Nueces County Office of Emergency Management
text: Nueces County Emergency Management Coordinator Lt. Col. Raymond Okafor-Williams announced today that the Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center handled about 2,900 emergency calls on Wednesday, September 15 — the busiest day in CBECC history and nearly ten times a normal day — and processed a record 2,109 rescue requests on Thursday, September 16, the most rescue calls the center has taken in a single day. The rescue surge was driven primarily by residents trapped by floodwater in Districts 3 and 4. 'Our dispatchers and the swift water rescue teams from Texas Task Force 1 worked through the night and into the next day to reach everyone who called,' said Okafor-Williams. 'We are proud of the professionalism shown by every member of the CBECC team.' On landfall day, Tuesday, September 14, the center took about 1,840 calls, about 1,100 of them rescue-related. Over the first three days of the storm response, CBECC handled more than 7,300 calls, compared to fewer than 1,000 calls during a normal three-day period. The center has sustained mutual aid staffing from San Patricio and Bee County, and anticipates call volume to remain elevated for several weeks as recovery operations continue.

issuer: FEMA Region 6
text: FEMA Region 6 today released preliminary damage assessment results based on the first systematic aerial drone survey of the Corpus Christi metropolitan area. A team of eight unmanned aircraft operated by Argus Aerial Systems under FEMA contract completed 180 square kilometers of coverage over residential and coastal zones between September 17 and 18. Based on automated structure analysis of approximately 847,000 image tiles, FEMA estimates between 4,200 and 5,800 structures in Nueces County sustained major or severe damage from Hurricane Rafael. These figures are preliminary and will be updated as the survey expands to additional zones, including the utility corridor and commercial districts. FEMA Federal Coordinating Officer Dennis Park said: 'The aerial survey gives us the most comprehensive picture we have had in the first days after a Gulf Coast hurricane. We are sharing these results directly with Nueces County emergency management and the City of Corpus Christi to inform resource deployment.' Additional survey phases targeting utility infrastructure and the Port of Corpus Christi are scheduled to begin within the week.

issuer: Unified Command (U.S. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi / Texas General Land Office) / TCEQ
text: UNIFIED COMMAND UPDATE — September 18, 2027: The Unified Command for the Inner Harbor oil spill confirms heavy shoreline oiling along Nueces Bay. Oil released from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as Hurricane Rafael arrived was carried out of the ship channel by surge and wind; sheen covers about 33 square miles of Nueces and Corpus Christi bays. A TCEQ water quality station in Nueces Bay recorded petroleum hydrocarbon levels of 2.1 mg/L this afternoon. Texas Parks and Wildlife biologists and personnel from the Coastal Bend Wildlife Rescue have documented 41 oiled birds along the Nueces Bay shoreline, including brown pelicans and laughing gulls. Wildlife rescue operations are underway. Because of the oil, Texas Parks and Wildlife has closed fishing and the Texas Department of State Health Services has closed shellfish harvesting in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays, effective immediately and until further notice. Additional containment boom is being placed at the Nueces Bay Causeway channel. The Coast Guard expects to issue its formal responsible-party designation within 72 hours. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

issuer: CCFD / US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi joint briefing
text: Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center Dispatch Chief Elena Vasquez-Okafor and Coast Guard Sector Commander Delia Ostrowski-Han announced today that mass rescue operations in the Corpus Christi area have concluded, with 1,427 confirmed rescues over five days. The operation involved 34 coordinated teams at peak, including US Coast Guard, Texas Task Force 1, Corpus Christi Fire Department, Nueces County Sheriff Search and Rescue, and 87 credentialed civilian boat operators. Search teams recovered two bodies during the operation, both occupants of a submerged vehicle on Violet Road; the county's confirmed storm death toll stands at 23. Chief Vasquez-Okafor praised the performance of contracted UAS operators whose thermal imaging capabilities enabled the identification of survivors in darkness and debris. Commander Ostrowski-Han noted that this was the largest helicopter hoist rescue operation in Corpus Christi history. Remaining SAR resources will transition to welfare check mode; residents who have not yet been contacted by a welfare check team should call 211.

issuer: USCG Sector Corpus Christi
text: The United States Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi confirms that marine inspectors and pollution investigators completed inspections aboard MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth yesterday, September 19, 2027. Both crews are safe. Both vessels remain moored under a Captain of the Port order and will not move until the investigation and the owners' obligations under federal oil spill law are addressed. Investigators documented the condition of the cargo systems on both ships and are examining possible unauthorized remote access to the tankers' cargo-control systems, with federal cyber teams assisting. The Coast Guard will not characterize the cause of the release while the investigation is open. The oil spill response continues, with containment boom deployed along affected shoreline in Nueces and Corpus Christi bays.

issuer: US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi
text: The US Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi has submitted its formal Incident Summary Report for Operation Rafael SAR (ISR-2027-CC-004) to Coast Guard District 8. The report certifies 1,427 total rescues: 341 by helicopter hoist, 1,041 by surface vessel (Coast Guard, state, and civilian), and 45 ambulatory survivor contacts. The report notes that contracted unmanned aerial system operators provided 112 thermal imaging annotations directly used to coordinate surface rescue operations. The Coast Guard thanks the community of Corpus Christi and all mutual-aid partners for their outstanding response. A formal after-action review will be conducted within 90 days.

issuer: U.S. Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi (Federal On-Scene Coordinator)
text: RESPONSIBLE PARTIES DESIGNATED — September 21, 2027: The U.S. Coast Guard, as Federal On-Scene Coordinator for the September 14 Inner Harbor oil release, has formally designated the owners of the tankers MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay as responsible parties under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. Oil fingerprint analysis by the Coast Guard confirms that oil samples collected in the Inner Harbor, Corpus Christi Bay and Nueces Bay match the crude oil cargoes aboard the two vessels. The owners have been issued Notices of Federal Interest and are required to fund cleanup and to set up a process for damage claims. The estimated discharge remains about 9,000 barrels of crude oil. To keep response contractors working without interruption, the Coast Guard has opened the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund with an initial ceiling of $4.2 million, to be recovered from the responsible parties. The designation assigns financial responsibility for the response; it is not a finding on the cause of the release, which remains under investigation. Contact: Unified Command Joint Information Center (JIC), (361) 555-0147.

issuer: City of Corpus Christi Water Department
text: The City of Corpus Christi Water Department has issued a boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4, effective immediately. Low water pressure in the distribution system serving the two districts — a consequence of storm damage to treatment and pumping infrastructure — means that contamination cannot be ruled out. Approximately 48,000 residents are affected. All tap water must be brought to a rolling boil for two minutes before drinking or cooking until further notice.

issuer: Corpus Christi Water Department / Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
text: BOIL WATER NOTICE — Districts 3 and 4. Effective immediately, all residents and businesses served by the City of Corpus Christi water system in Water Districts 3 and 4 (ZIP codes 78401, 78405, 78407, 78408, 78416 and 78417) are advised to boil all water used for drinking, cooking, and making ice. This notice is issued due to low system pressure in these districts following Hurricane Rafael damage to distribution infrastructure. To make water safe: bring water to a rolling boil for two minutes before use. This notice affects approximately 48,000 residents. Updates will be issued through the City's emergency notification system, local television and local radio. For more information call 361-826-1600.

issuer: Nueces County Office of Emergency Management / City of Corpus Christi
text: The Coastal Bend Emergency Communications Center is experiencing a significant increase in calls related to today's boil water notice for Districts 3 and 4. CBECC Director Patricia Escamilla-Voss urges residents with water safety questions to call the newly established NuecesInfoLine at 361-826-INFO rather than 911. '911 is for life-threatening emergencies only,' Director Escamilla-Voss said. 'The NuecesInfoLine has operators available to answer your questions about the boil water notice, water distribution sites, and when water service is expected to be restored — please use that number and keep 911 available for people whose lives are in danger.' The NuecesInfoLine is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Information is also available in Spanish by pressing 2. Water distribution sites are open at the Tuloso-Midway High School gym, the Woodlawn Community Center, and Cefe Valenzuela Park; hours and addresses are listed at the City of Corpus Christi emergency management website.

issuer: Bayside Ledger
text: Spanish-speaking residents of Districts 3 and 4 did not receive the city's boil-water notice until more than 12 hours after English-language alerts went out Sunday evening, the Bayside Ledger has confirmed. The notice, issued at 5:30 p.m. Sunday, reached KNCB Coastal Bend Radio — the primary news source for an estimated 34,000 Spanish-speaking listeners in Corpus Christi — only at 6:03 Monday morning. 'We received the official notice from the city this morning,' KNCB news director Marisol Fuentes-Vega said Monday. 'By then many of our listeners had already been using untreated water overnight.' Nueces County Office of Emergency Management spokesperson Cassandra Trejo-Morales confirmed the delay, attributing it to reduced staffing at the county's translation contractor, Nueces County Language Access Services. 'We are reviewing what happened and what can be done differently,' Trejo-Morales said. The boil-water notice covers approximately 48,000 residents and remained in effect as of press time.

issuer: Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
text: Restoration crews working in Corpus Christi have encountered cascading substation failures in the northwest and central districts that are extending the recovery timeline beyond initial estimates. Crews are on-site at two facilities to investigate protective relay conditions exacerbated by storm debris. We expect the final 32,000 affected customers in those areas to be restored within 7 to 10 days. We appreciate their patience.

issuer: FEMA Region 6 / Texas Division of Emergency Management
text: FEMA's Mitigation Assessment Team today released the Phase 2 Utility Infrastructure Aerial Survey Summary for the Corpus Christi Hurricane Rafael response. The survey, completed over September 23 through 26, covered 23 utility infrastructure sites including five CBPWA electrical substations, the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant, four pumping stations, and nine telecommunications relay facilities. The assessment found visible storm damage at 14 of the 23 sites, with the O.N. Stevens plant sustaining moderate roof damage to the C-pump station. The report identifies two CBPWA substations — Harbor View and Crosstown — as requiring follow-up engineering inspection due to equipment configurations observed in the imagery. Texas Division of Emergency Management Infrastructure Division Chief Rafael Montoya-Chen said: 'The aerial survey has given engineers a roadmap so that when crews reach those sites, they know what to look for and can prioritize the most critical restoration steps.' The full Phase 2 imagery set is available to credentialed government users through the FEMA GeoPlatform.

issuer: FAA and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations
text: The Federal Aviation Administration and US Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations today confirmed that investigators have identified multiple incidents of unauthorized unmanned aircraft system operations in the Corpus Christi area during the period preceding Hurricane Rafael. The aircraft operated without required FAA authorizations and were detected through a combination of radar and electronic sensor records. CBP Air and Marine Operations Corpus Christi (CAMCC) and the US Coast Guard are coordinating with the FAA and appropriate law enforcement agencies. Due to the ongoing nature of the investigation, no additional details about the number, location, or timing of the incidents can be released at this time. CBP and FAA jointly urge any members of the public with information about unauthorized drone operations in the Corpus Christi area between September 4 and September 12, 2027, to contact the FBI field office at 361-888-3111.

issuer: Texas Department of Public Safety
text: CONTRACTOR FRAUD ALERT — September 29, 2027: The Texas Department of Public Safety is issuing an urgent consumer alert following more than 300 complaints about fraudulent water damage contractors in the Corpus Christi area since Hurricane Rafael. Residents in Districts 3 and 4, particularly those affected by flooding and water damage from the storm, are most at risk. Specific complaints include contractors charging for water extraction, mold remediation, and drywall repair at prices 3 to 5 times above normal market rates; charging for services never performed; using forged insurance adjuster documentation; and requesting victims sign over assignment-of-benefits rights to allow direct billing to insurance carriers without homeowner review. DPS urges residents to: verify contractor license at license.state.tx.us; get minimum three written estimates; never sign assignment-of-benefits without reading the full document; pay only after work is completed and inspected. Any resident who believes they have been victimized should contact Texas DPS at (512) 424-2000 or local law enforcement. This warning applies to all contractors, including those offering emergency water damage restoration services.

issuer: Northlight Threat Lab
text: Threat researcher finds rumor posts were coordinated across about 40 accounts and linked to the same lookalike aid site used in phishing emails (aid-help-portal.example).

issuer: Gulfwater Maritime Report
text: Gulfwater Maritime Report has confirmed with sources familiar with the investigation that federal authorities are examining whether commercial drones conducted surveillance flights over the Port of Corpus Christi and at least one local power utility facility in the days before Hurricane Rafael. Sources say the flights were detected through radar records maintained by the Coast Guard. No organization has claimed responsibility. The timing of the flights — the week before Hurricane Rafael landfall — has drawn attention from investigators given subsequent damage to critical infrastructure during and after the storm. The FBI has asked for public tips.
